title: Credit Control
description:
Credit Controller (Part-Time)

Wrexham Hybrid Working 20 Hours Per Week 12-Month Contract

We're working with a growing and successful business based in Wrexham that is looking to add a Debtors Clerk to its finance team on a part-time basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys building relationships, keeping accounts on track, and playing a key role in maintaining healthy cash flow. You'll be joining a supportive team where your contribution will make a real difference to the business.

Reporting to the Accounts Manager, you'll be responsible for managing customer accounts, recovering outstanding payments, and ensuring financial records remain accurate and up to date.

What You'll Be Doing
- Managing customer accounts and monitoring outstanding balances
- Issuing invoices, statements and payment reminders
- Following up on overdue accounts and maintaining accurate collection records
- Reconciling customer accounts and resolving payment queries
- Processing and allocating incoming payments
- Producing aged debt reports and supporting cash flow activities
- Building positive relationships with customers while ensuring payments are received on time
- Managing customer credit limits
- Processing credit notes and account adjustments
- Handling prepayments and releasing orders where required
- Completing online payment reconciliations

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience within credit control, debt recovery, or accounts receivable
- Strong attention to detail and excellent record-keeping skills
- Good problem-solving abilities and a practical approach to resolving issues
- Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, lookups and pivot tables
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal
- Ability to manage your workload independently and prioritise effectively

Desirable Experience
- At least 12 months' experience in a similar role
- Experience using ERP or finance systems
- A good understanding of the full debtor management process

Working Hours

20 hours per week across 5 days, worked flexibly:
- Monday to Thursday between 9:00am and 5:00pm
- Friday between 8:00am and 4:00pm

Contract
- Initial 12-month contract
- Potential for extension or a permanent opportunity

What's In It For You?
- 28 days holiday, including bank holidays (pro rata)
- Company pension scheme
- Private healthcare support
- Free annual eye test voucher
- Free annual flu jab
- Mental health and wellbeing support
- Regular social and team events
- Free on-site parking
- Supportive and collaborative working environment
- Hybrid working with a minimum of two office days per week

Salary

Competitive salary available upon application.

title: HR Administrator
description:
Your new company
You will be working with a growing education provider in the Wrexham area.
Your new role
Working in a large HR and People Operations function, you will provide administrative support to HR Officers and the wider team! Based on site in Wrexham, you will be assisting with a range of administrative duties, such as right to work checks, processing of DBS checks where necessary, updating and maintaining personnel and employee information, processing sick leave and parental leave, responding to administrative enquiries from a shared inbox, as well as maintaining accurate records on the HR database! Prior experience as a HR administrator or a HR assistant will be essential to hit the ground running for this post! Ideally, you will be experienced in all administrative duties for on and offboarding processes, ER considerations and be used to maintaining databases with discretion. You will be using your excellent attention to detail daily to ensure processes are conducted appropriately, and be comfortable putting your strong communication skills to good use daily in written and verbal formats. You will be immediately available and be able to bring your positive work attitude at short notice! You must be locally situated to Wrexham for this site based role.
What you'll get in return
Working for 9 months with a local employer of choice, you will have a stable temporary contract which will take you through to Summer of 2027. You will have access to free on site parking, excellent on site amenities, and full time hours for the duration! You will have a pay rate of 14.50ph

description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Unison Branch Administrator to work within the North Wales Police Force

Our client, a prominent organisation in the public services sector, is seeking a dedicated Unison Branch Administrator to join their team in Colwyn Bay. This part-time 18.5 hours per week Monday to Friday role offers an hourly rate of 14.10 per hour and is set to run until March, 2027. The successful candidate will play a key role in providing essential administrative support to the North Wales Police UNISON Branch.

Key Responsibilities:

As a Unison Branch Administrator, the responsibilities will include:
- Performing general administrative duties such as word processing, formatting documents, and managing diaries.
- Responding to inquiries from both internal and external sources with professionalism and efficiency.
- Organising, scheduling, and attending events, meetings, and conferences for the North Wales Police and UNISON.
- Preparing agendas and taking minutes to ensure smooth communication within the organisation.
- Making travel arrangements for branch officers and representatives, utilising the Atriis system.
- Managing and distributing UNISON information leaflets and merchandise.

- Previous experience in providing administrative support, including meeting preparation and minute-taking.

Job Advert: Finance and Creditors Administrator

Location: Colwyn Bay
Contract Type: Temporary
Hourly Rate: 14.10
Working Pattern: Full Time - Hybrid

Our client, North Wales Police are seeking a diligent and proactive Finance and Creditors Administrator to join their dynamic Purchasing and Creditors Team. This position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to the financial and administrative support functions in a fast-paced environment, all while ensuring top-tier customer service.

title: IT Projects Administrator
description:
Job Title: Projects Administrator

Location: St Asaph - Onsite

Salary: 26,000 - 28,000 per annum

Job Type: Full-time, Permanent

Ready to take the first step in your project career? We're looking for a driven, highly organised and enthusiastic Projects administrator to join our growing team, with plenty of opportunity to learn, develop and progress in one of the UK's fastest-growing MSPs.

About Flotek:

Flotek Group is the UK's fastest-growing Managed Service Providers, delivering IT, Cyber Security, Communications and Managed Print solutions to small and medium-sized businesses. With regional sales and support hubs across the UK, our ambitious growth story is built on a simple foundation: every product and service we deliver is backed by expertise, passion and heart. We're a values-led business, and our people are at the centre of everything we do.

About The Role:

We're looking for a highly accurate individual with a keen eye for detail who enjoys a fast pace of work. You will play a key role in supporting our Engineers ensuring the smooth delivery of installations from start to finish. Excellent communication is essential as you'll need to communicate with internal and external stakeholders. You'll also be responsible for coordinating stock and documentation as well as managing engineers' diaries to schedule installations.

Day-to-day activities include:
- Raising and managing purchase orders, ensuring stock is tracked and allocated to the correct projects
- Answering incoming calls to the Projects queue
- Managing all incoming and outgoing stock
- Coordinating engineer documentation - permits, job packs and completion photos
- Scheduling engineers' diaries and allocating resources across projects
- Working closely with the Billing and Finance team to meet strict invoicing deadlines and ensure all financial documentation is accurate and submitted on time
- Scheduling deliveries and site access for Engineering
- Providing day-to-day administrative support to the Projects Team Managers

Skills / Experience:
- Microsoft office including Excel - knowledge of analysing data and Excel functions
- Previous use of CRM/PSA software
- Experience in a similar role within the data cabling, IT or telecoms industry (preferred)
- Stock management

Benefits:
- Opportunities for professional growth and development.
- Staff Share Equity Scheme - your piece of the "Purple Pie"
- 21 Days Holiday increasing to 25 with 4 years of service (+ bank holidays)
- Your birthday off

Due to the nature of the role the company will not be able to offer sponsorship or relocation assistance so candidates must already reside in the UK.

Please click the APPLY button to submit your CV for this role.

Candidates with the experience or relevant job titles of; IT Project Operations Administrator, MSP Projects & Logistics Administrator, IT Project Coordinator, MSP Project Coordinator may also be considered for this role.

title: Office and Contract Administrator
description:
Office and Contract Administrator
Location: Mold, North Wales
Salary: 27,000 - 29,000 per annum (depending on experience)
Hours: Monday to Friday, 8:30am - 4:30pm
Our client is a well-established, family-run business specialising in grounds maintenance, landscaping and tree work services across North Wales and surrounding areas.
Due to continued growth, they are looking to recruit an experienced and organised Office & Contracts Administrator to provide essential support to the Directors and Management team. This is a varied role combining office administration, contract support, client liaison and the coordination of business-critical paperwork and processes.
The Role
As Office & Contracts Administrator, you will play a key role in ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the business. You will manage administrative processes, support contract delivery, coordinate documentation and act as a professional point of contact for clients, suppliers and subcontractors.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership of their workload, has strong organisational skills and can confidently manage multiple priorities in a busy office environment.

Client Liaison & Contract Administration
Act as a key point of contact for clients via telephone and email.
Support managers with scheduling and work coordination.
Liaise with clients, subcontractors and site contacts regarding access arrangements and availability.
Confirm work schedules and keep clients updated on any changes.
Maintain accurate contract records, visit schedules and client information.
Prepare and issue correspondence, reports and supporting documentation.
Record and track customer enquiries, concerns and complaints, ensuring appropriate follow-up.

Prepare documentation to support invoicing and resolve related administrative queries.
Office & Business Support

Maintain electronic filing systems, spreadsheets, diaries and action trackers.
Monitor contract, insurance and company renewal dates.
Assist with audits, assessments and accreditation requirements.
Maintain company policies, procedures and compliance records.
Support employee administration, including onboarding paperwork, training records and timesheets.
Arrange meetings, prepare documentation and record actions where required.
Order office supplies and provide general administrative support to the leadership team.
Requirements
Previous experience within a busy office administration role.
Excellent organisational skills and strong attention to detail.
Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines.
Confident and professional communication skills.
Strong IT skills including Microsoft Office and Excel.
Ability to work independently and use initiative.
A practical and logical approach to problem-solving.
Professional and confidential approach when handling sensitive information.
Desirable Experience
Contract administration experience.
Purchasing or supplier coordination experience.
Compliance or accreditation administration.
Employee administration, training records or payroll support.
Experience working within construction, grounds maintenance, engineering or field-based service environments.

title: Operations & Fulfilment Coordinator (Part Time)
description:
Job Description Operations Coordinator

Role at a glance

Hours:- 24 Hours per week, three full days, or spread across Monday to Friday by agreement

Location:- Flint, Mainly on site, with scope for some hybrid working once established

Salary:- £15.25 p/h

Contract:- Permanent, Part Time

About us

We are a small team where everyone's work matters and good ideas are acted on quickly.

The role

This is a hands-on role that combines purchasing, order administration and warehouse work. You will make sure customer orders are bought in, checked, packed and dispatched correctly and on time.

Over time you will take ownership of the day-to-day operational work currently handled by the Director, so that problems are picked up and solved without needing to be escalated.

For the successful candidate there will be growth opportunities.

Key responsibilities

Purchasing
- Raise purchase orders from the sales orders and check them for accuracy.
- Send purchase orders to our manufacturers with the required due dates.
- Check order confirmations against the dates and prices. Chase corrections where needed and update the system.
- Keep prices on purchase orders accurate and up to date.

Sales orders and dispatch
- Liaise with customers on product specifications and order details, working with the Directors where needed.
- Adjust and finalise sales orders so they are correct and ready to invoice before dispatch.

Warehouse
- Handle goods in and goods out.
